ENV['COCOAPODS_DISABLE_STATS'] = 'true'

project 'Runner', {
  'Debug' => :debug,
  'Profile' => :release,
  'Release' => :release,
}

def flutter_root
  generated_xcode_build_settings_path = File.expand_path(File.join('..', 'Flutter', 'Generated.xcconfig'), __FILE__)
  unless File.exist?(generated_xcode_build_settings_path)
    raise "#{generated_xcode_build_settings_path} must exist. If you're running pod install manually, make sure flutter pub get is executed first"
  end

  File.foreach(generated_xcode_build_settings_path) do |line|
    matches = line.match(/FLUTTER_ROOT\=(.*)/)
    return matches[1].strip if matches
  end
  raise "FLUTTER_ROOT not found in #{generated_xcode_build_settings_path}. Try deleting Generated.xcconfig, then run flutter pub get"
end

require File.expand_path(File.join('packages', 'flutter_tools', 'bin', 'podhelper'), flutter_root)

flutter_ios_podfile_setup

target 'Runner' do
  # Statically linked pods: the validated configuration for this app's
  # pods (kept after the on-device Gemma removal — gh-2004; its LiteRT-LM
  # native-asset frameworks motivated the original switch).
  use_frameworks! :linkage => :static

  flutter_install_all_ios_pods File.dirname(File.realpath(__FILE__))
  target 'RunnerTests' do
    inherit! :search_paths
  end
end

post_install do |installer|
  installer.pods_project.targets.each do |target|
    flutter_additional_ios_build_settings(target)
  end

  # wasm_run FFI symbols live in a static library inside WasmRun.xcframework.
  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because
  # DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=YES (Release default) still discards the unreferenced
  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive
  # itself so the list stays in sync with the vendored package. Without this
  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen
  # ("Unsupported desktop platform: ios" from wasm_run's library locator).
  # SRCROOT is the ios/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where
  # vendor/ lives.
  xcframework = '$(SRCROOT)/../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework'
  device_slice = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64/libwasm_run_dart.a"
  simulator_slice = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libwasm_run_dart.a"
  device_archive = File.expand_path('../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/ios-arm64/libwasm_run_dart.a', __dir__)
  ffi_symbols = `nm -gU -arch arm64 #{device_archive}`.lines
    .map(&:split)
    .select { |cols| %w[T D S].include?(cols[1]) && cols[2] }
    .map { |cols| cols[2] }
    .uniq
    .grep(/^_(wire|new|drop|free|get|store|init|inflate|share)_/)
    .sort
  raise "no wasm_run FFI symbols found in #{device_archive}" if ffi_symbols.empty?
  export_flags = ffi_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,#{s}" }
  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|
    aggregate_target.user_project.targets.each do |target|
      next unless target.name == 'Runner'
      target.build_configurations.each do |config|
        # Archive/install builds run `strip` per STRIP_STYLE. The default
        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely (verified: plain
        # `strip` drops every exported wire_* symbol), which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        { 'iphoneos*' => device_slice, 'iphonesimulator*' => simulator_slice }.each do |sdk, slice|
          key = "OTHER_LDFLAGS[sdk=#{sdk}]"
          ldflags = Array(config.build_settings[key] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
          # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
          ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
          ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{slice}"
          # cupertino_http (the NSURLSession-backed HTTP client on iOS)
          # ships its FFI trampolines (_NativeCupertinoHttp_*) in a static
          # pod framework. Nothing native references them, so the Release
          # link dead-strips the archive members and Dart's dlsym lookup
          # fails at runtime ('No asset with id package:cupertino_http/
          # src/native_cupertino_bindings.dart found') — every network call
          # errors out. Same failure class as the wasm_run white screen.
          #
          # The fix is -exported_symbol, NOT force_load: an exported symbol
          # must exist in the output, so ld pulls the defining archive
          # member AND keeps it in the exports trie (which is what dlsym
          # reads). force_load of the same archive the pod already links
          # via -framework would double-include the dummy object
          # (duplicate PodsDummy_cupertino_http) — and breaking the
          # -framework flag instead would drop the pod-target build
          # ordering ('Build input file cannot be found' under gym's
          # archive build). Both failure modes seen on CI.
          #
          # The symbols are derived from the plugin's generated bindings
          # source (C names gain one Mach-O underscore, hence the extra '_').
          # Drop cupertino_http force_load flags injected by earlier
          # Podfile revisions — exported_symbol alone is the fix now.
          ldflags.reject! { |f| f.include?('cupertino_http') && f.start_with?('-Wl,-force_load') }
          cupertino_src = File.expand_path(
            '.symlinks/plugins/cupertino_http/darwin/cupertino_http/Sources/cupertino_http/native_cupertino_bindings.m',
            __dir__,
          )
          cupertino_symbols = File.read(cupertino_src)
            .scan(/\b_NativeCupertinoHttp_\w+/)
            .uniq
            .sort
          raise "no _NativeCupertinoHttp_* symbols found in #{cupertino_src}" if cupertino_symbols.empty?
          cupertino_export_flags = cupertino_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,_#{s}" }
          ldflags.reject! { |f| f.include?('_NativeCupertinoHttp_') }
          if config.name == 'Debug'
            # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
            # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
            # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
            # at launch. But WITHOUT any flag the trampoline archive members
            # are never pulled either (nothing native references them), so
            # Dart's dlsym fallback fails at runtime even in Debug.
            # -Wl,-u,<sym> forces the defining members into the link while
            # leaving the default "export all globals" trie intact.
            ldflags.concat(cupertino_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-u,_#{s}" })
          else
            ldflags.concat(cupertino_export_flags)
          end
          ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
          config.build_settings[key] = ldflags
        end
      end
    end
  end

  # The vendored WasmRun.xcframework only ships an arm64 simulator slice.
  # Exclude x86_64 simulator everywhere so Debug simulator builds do not try
  # to link a missing slice.
  exclude_x86_64_sim = { 'EXCLUDED_ARCHS[sdk=iphonesimulator*]' => 'x86_64' }

  # iOS 16 floor everywhere (pods + app target).
  # Project-level configs alone are not enough: pod TARGET-level build
  # settings (declared by podspecs, e.g. Firebase's 15.0) override them, and
  # newer Swift toolchains error when a 15.0 target imports a module built
  # for 16.0 (Promises) — seen after the Flutter SDK bump.
  installer.pods_project.targets.each do |target|
    target.build_configurations.each do |config|
      config.build_settings['IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET'] = '16.0'
    end
  end
  installer.pods_project.build_configurations.each do |config|
    config.build_settings['IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET'] = '16.0'
    exclude_x86_64_sim.each { |k, v| config.build_settings[k] = v }
  end

  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|
    aggregate_target.user_project.build_configurations.each do |config|
      config.build_settings['IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET'] = '16.0'
      exclude_x86_64_sim.each { |k, v| config.build_settings[k] = v }
    end
    aggregate_target.user_targets.each do |user_target|
      user_target.build_configurations.each do |config|
        config.build_settings['IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET'] = '16.0'
        exclude_x86_64_sim.each { |k, v| config.build_settings[k] = v }
      end
    end
    aggregate_target.user_project.save
  end
end

Now I see the structure. There are two forms in the committed pbxproj:

1. `OTHER_LDFLAGS = ("$(inherited)", "-force_load", "<path>");` — this is the OLD style (bare `-force_load` followed by path).
2. `"OTHER_LDFLAGS[sdk=iphoneos*]" = (..., "-Wl,-force_load,<path>", "-Wl,-exported_symbol,...")` — the NEW style written by the Podfile post_install hook.

The committed pbxproj has both. The Podfile's post_install, at pod-install time, strips `f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a')` from `OTHER_LDFLAGS[sdk=...]` keys only — it does NOT touch the plain `OTHER_LDFLAGS` (no sdk qualifier) list! Look at the code:

``
{ 'iphoneos*' => device_slice, 'iphonesimulator*' => simulator_slice }.each do |sdk, slice|
 key = "OTHER_LDFLAGS[sdk=#{sdk}]"
 ldflags = Array(config.build_settings[key] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
 ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
 ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{slice}"

release_tag_name = 'wasm_run-v0.1.0' # generated; do not edit

# We cannot distribute the XCFramework alongside the library directly,
# so we have to fetch the correct version here.
framework_name = 'WasmRun.xcframework'
remote_zip_name = "#{framework_name}.zip"
url = "https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/#{release_tag_name}/#{remote_zip_name}"
local_zip_name = "#{release_tag_name}.zip"
# gh-2055 review round 2: Ruby does NOT check a bare backtick's exit status —
# `$?` is set but nothing reads it, so the shell block's own abort
# ("curl ... || exit 1") never propagated into pod install: a cold-tree
# failed download proceeded past the fetch and died at the Podfile
# post_install `nm` check with the root cause one screen up. Assigning the
# result and raising on `$?.success?` fails pod install AT the fetch step,
# with the curl error and the "wasm_run download failed" marker directly
# above it in the log. The raise reads `$?` on the line right after the
# closing backtick so no intervening child process can clobber the status.
fetch_output = `
cd Frameworks

# gh-2055: the guard must key on the artifact pod install actually consumes —
# the exact archive flutter_app/macos/Podfile force_loads and nm-checks —
# NOT on the downloaded-zip marker. A fresh CI clone never has the marker,
# so the old "if [ ! -f <zip> ]" guard made this block run on EVERY build:
# it removed the WasmRun.xcframework the build-macos.yml "Restore vendored
# WasmRun macOS framework" step had already placed (cache → local copy →
# digest-verified resumable download, gh-1149/gh-1759), re-downloaded the
# 92.7 MB asset with a bare curl, and one transient reset ("curl: (56)
# Recv failure: Connection reset by peer", daily leg run 41778615815) left
# pod install with NO framework — the Podfile nm check then failed on the
# missing libwasm_run_dart.a. With the archive in place this block is now
# a no-op; it stays as the local-dev fallback for a truly cold tree.
# --fail keeps an HTTP error page from masquerading as a zip (the same
# posture the workflow restore step is linted for); the || guard fails the
# block AT the curl step so a dead download surfaces its own error instead
# of being swallowed into unzip/truncate residue and the downstream
# Podfile nm diagnostic (gh-2055 review).
if [ ! -f #{framework_name}/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a ]
then
  rm -rf #{framework_name}
  curl --fail -L #{url} -o #{local_zip_name} || { echo "wasm_run download failed" >&2; exit 1; }
  unzip #{local_zip_name}
  truncate -s 0 #{local_zip_name}
  rm -rf #{framework_name}/ios-*
fi

cd -
`
raise "wasm_run framework fetch failed (see curl error above)" unless $?.success?

Pod::Spec.new do |s|
  s.name          = 'wasm_run_flutter'
  s.version       = '0.0.1'
  s.summary       = 'iOS/macOS Flutter bindings for wasm_run'
  s.license       = { :file => '../LICENSE' }
  s.homepage      = 'https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run'
  s.authors       = { 'Juan Manuel Castillo' => '42351046+juancastillo0@users.noreply.github.com' }

  # This pod is HEADER-ONLY on macOS (#1096 AC4): Classes/ keeps just
  # frb.h — EnforceBundling.swift was REMOVED because it is an iOS
  # mechanism (there the app statically links the pod's vendored
  # framework and the dummy keeps dead-code stripping from discarding
  # the wire_* roots). With no vendored framework, the pod target links
  # nothing that defines the flutter_rust_bridge symbols the dummy
  # references, so compiling it fails the pod-target link ("Undefined
  # symbols for architecture arm64 … in EnforceBundling.o"). On macOS
  # the app resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on its OWN
  # executable — Runner.xcodeproj force_loads
  # WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a and
  # exports the _wire_* symbols (CI verifies them per build) — so no
  # EnforceBundling dummy is needed. The embedded dynamic
  # wasm_run_flutter.framework (27 MB unpacked) was a never-loaded
  # fallback; vendoring it here is what put it in Frameworks/. The
  # XCFramework download block above STAYS — the static archive inside
  # it feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check.
  s.source              = { :path => '.' }
  s.source_files        = 'Classes/**/*'
  s.public_header_files = 'Classes/**/*.h'

  s.ios.deployment_target = '11.0'
  s.osx.deployment_target = '10.13'
end

);
``

- `-force_load` then the path → force_load the archive (old style)

content.text:
previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`
  jobs (the release publishes at the provenance step). `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
  `package-lock.json`s, and `vendor/wasm_run/native/Cargo.lock`); a listed
  lockfile that is missing/untracked/gitignored fails the Static gates, and
  pod-sync (flutter-analyze + nightly build legs, after `pub get`) fails
  when a native iOS/macOS plugin resolved by pubspec.lock has no pod in the
  platform's `Podfile.lock` (the gh-1274 class), or its pod is pinned at a
  stale version vs the resolved plugin podspec's `s.version` (the
  historical flutter_gemma 1.8.0-vs-1.11.3 skew; the podspec is the comparison target,
  not the pubspec version — vendored/beta pods legitimately differ from the
  Dart package version). The inventory also enforces the gh-1303 path-pin
  sync: `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` pins this repo as a path dependency, so
  its `flutter_agent_harness` pin must EXIST and equal the root
  `pubspec.yaml` version — a stale OR MISSING pin (e.g. a merge conflict
  resolved by dropping the entry) makes every
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` consumer red — the pins are
  `0.0.0-dev` on both sides and NEVER churn across releases (gh-1522: the
  tag is the version; the release flow mutates zero files), and the Static
  gate catches any other path to the drift at PR time. After ANY pubspec.yaml
  dependency change that adds/updates a darwin-native plugin: `cd
  flutter_app/ios && pod install --repo-update` and the same in `macos/`,
  commit both `Podfile.lock`s (CocoaPods runs fine on Linux for
  regeneration; the wasm_run `nm` step needs an llvm-nm shim + the
  XCFramework staged via `scripts/setup_vendor_ios.sh` or the upstream zip).
  Guard red exits are fixture-self-tested (`scripts/
  check_lockfiles_selftest.sh`, Static gates).

content.text:
Closes #2070
### Root Cause
`Cube kernel live (macOS)` was killed by its own `timeout-minutes: 10` while its first step — a plain github.com `actions/checkout` — was still stalled (9m32s against a 1–3 s baseline; 8 observed runs have full-job walls of 68–114 s). The job concluded `cancelled`, the platform-leg verdict in `Quality gate` reds on anything not success/skipped (#1368), and the release train died downstream: `Auto-release` skipped, provenance never signed, and `Advance vpinned marker` refused to move the marker by design (`pin_release.sh` fail-closed without signed SHA256SUMS). The stall is the documented fa-m5 contention class (gh-2013: ONE host hosting three runner registrations); the ceiling was the tightest on the box and sized to the healthy wall.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`cube-kernel-live`): `timeout-minutes` 10 → 30 — clears the gh-2070 stall with ~20 min of slack, at the sibling hosted-macos leg class (`build-ios`: 30); a genuinely wedged box still fails loudly, just later. Same structural remedy as gh-1778 (test-core budget, v1.0.621).
- `test/ci_cube_kernel_ceiling_guard_test.dart` (new): YAML-level guard pinning AC1 job ceiling ≥ 30, AC2 the leg stays on the `macos-m5` pool, AC3 no step-level `timeout-minutes` under the ceiling reintroduces the kill.

### Test Coverage
- `test/ci_cube_kernel_ceiling_guard_test.dart` — verified RED pre-fix (AC1: expected ≥ 30, actual 10), GREEN post-fix: 3/3 passed.
- Workflow-shape suites against the edited `ci.yml`: `workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart`, `release_hygiene_test.dart`, `release_flow_race_test.dart`, `ci_core_shard_timeout_guard_test.dart`, `ci_macos_keychain_serialization_guard_test.dart` + 12 more `ci.yml`-parsing guard files — 246 tests passed, 0 failures.

### Notes
- No product-code change; the cube/keychain tests themselves were green in every observed run. The pub.dev publish was unaffected (dart_ok stays true on platform-only red) — v1.0.695 is published; only the release train and the `vpinned` marker advance were lost to this red.
- Adjacent gaps observed but deliberately not fixed here (documented in `outputs/rca.md`): the degraded-runner watchdog is `pull_request`-only (tag runs have no retrigger) and its detector scans only `failure` jobs — a `timeout-minutes` kill concludes `cancelled` and is invisible to it; the mirror-checkout hardening used by the other self-hosted legs was not ported to this leg (needs new tag/PR-merge-ref handling — larger surface than this ticket warrants).

#!/bin/bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# Copies the prebuilt WasmRun.xcframework from the pub cache into the vendored
# wasm_run_flutter plugin. The Dart/Objective-C bridge in vendor/ was patched
# to remove unused capturedStdout/capturedStderr symbols, but the native binary
# is unchanged from the published package, so we reuse it from pub.dev.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

PUB_CACHE="${PUB_CACHE:-$HOME/.pub-cache}"
SOURCE="$PUB_CACHE/hosted/pub.dev/wasm_run_flutter-0.1.0/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
DEST="$REPO_ROOT/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"

if [[ ! -d "$SOURCE" ]]; then
  echo "Error: prebuilt XCFramework not found in pub cache: $SOURCE"
  echo "Run 'flutter pub get' in the example app first so the original package is cached."
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DEST")"
rm -rf "$DEST"
cp -R "$SOURCE" "$DEST"
echo "Copied WasmRun.xcframework to $DEST"

{

{
  case "$1" in
  "WasmRun.xcframework/ios-arm64")

    echo "arm64 x86_64"
    ;;

}

{

local xcframework_name="$1"
  xcframework_name="${xcframework_name##*/}"
  local paths=("${@:2}")
  # Locate the correct slice of the .xcframework for the current architectures
  local target_path=""

  # Split archs on space so we can find a slice that has all the needed archs
  local target_archs=$(echo $ARCHS | tr " " "\n")

  local target_variant=""
  if [[ "$PLATFORM_NAME" == *"simulator" ]]; then
    target_variant="simulator"
  fi
  if [[ ! -z ${EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME+x} && "$EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME" == *"maccatalyst" ]]; then
    target_variant="maccatalyst"
  fi
  for i in ${!paths[@]}; do
    local matched_all_archs="1"
    local slice_archs="$(archs_for_slice "${xcframework_name}/${paths[$i]}")"
    local slice_variant="$(variant_for_slice "${xcframework_name}/${paths[$i]}")"
    for target_arch in $target_archs; do
      if ! [[ "${slice_variant}" == "$target_variant" ]]; then
        matched_all_archs="0"
        break
      fi

      if ! echo "${slice_archs}" | tr " " "\n" | grep -F -q -x "$target_arch"; then
        matched_all_archs="0"
        break
      fi
    done

    if [[ "$matched_all_archs" == "1" ]]; then
      # Found a matching slice
      echo "Selected xcframework slice ${paths[$i]}"
      SELECT_SLICE_RETVAL=${paths[$i]}
      break
    fi
  done
}

install_xcframework() {
  local basepath="$1"
  local name="$2"
  local package_type="$3"
  local paths=("${@:4}")

  # Locate the correct slice of the .xcframework for the current architectures
  select_slice "${basepath}" "${paths[@]}"
  local target_path="$SELECT_SLICE_RETVAL"
  if [[ -z "$target_path" ]]; then
    echo "warning: [CP] $(basename ${basepath}): Unable to find matching slice in '${paths[@]}' for the current build architectures ($ARCHS) and platform (${EFFECTIVE_PLATFORM_NAME-${PLATFORM_NAME}})."
    return
  fi
  local source="$basepath/$target_path"

  local destination="${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/${name}"

  if [ ! -d "$destination" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$destination"
  fi

  copy_dir "$source/" "$destination"
  echo "Copied $source to $destination"
}

install_xcframework "${PODS_ROOT}/../.symlinks/plugins/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework" "wasm_run_flutter" "library" "ios-arm64" "ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"

Confirmed the mechanism:

**"[CP] Copy XCFrameworks"** phase of the wasm_run_flutter pod target:
- **inputFileListPaths**: the xcframework at `.symlinks/plugins/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework`
- **outputFileListPaths**: `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter/WasmRun.framework` — **a file the script NEVER produces** (the slice holds a bare `libwasm_run_dart.a`, no `WasmRun.framework` bundle!)

Xcode script-phase up-to-date logic: run if (outputs missing) OR (any output older than any input). Since the declared output NEVER exists, the phase re-runs every build — normally. That's the healthy path (fa-m5-1, hosted, fa-m5-2@19:52).

On fa-m5-2 since the canceled 20:45 run, the link fails to find `-lwasm_run_dart` in `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter` — 6/6 runs, three different trees. What box residue could cause "phase skipped" or "copy empty" persistently? A stale `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter/WasmRun.framework` directory — Xcode would SKIP the phase (outputs "present") IF the output's mtime ≥ input's mtime. The input xcframework is re-unzipped fresh each run (restore step) → input mtime = unzip time (fresh) → output (stale, older) < input → phase re-runs... 

**UNLESS the restore step's unzip PRESERVES the zip's internal mtimes — Nov 12 2023!!** Look at the `ls -la` output of the restored xcframework: ALL files dated "Nov 12 2023"! unzip restores ARCHIVE mtimes by default! # Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Build iOS (debug, unsigned)` CI leg fails at the Runner link with
`Error (Xcode): Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found`, red-ing the Quality gate
and stopping the v1.0.707 release train (vpinned provenance gate has no
release assets to pin).

**Root cause**: `flutter_app/ios/Podfile` + the vendored
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/wasm_run_flutter.podspec` leave the Runner app
link's `-l"wasm_run_dart"` flag (generated by CocoaPods from the
`vendored_frameworks` XCFramework) resolving **exclusively** through
`LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS = ${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter`
(`Pods/Target Support Files/Pods-Runner/Pods-Runner.debug.xcconfig`,
`PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR = $(PODS_CONFIGURATION_BUILD_DIR)/XCFrameworkIntermediates`).
That directory is populated only by the `wasm_run_flutter` pod target's
`[CP] Copy XCFrameworks` script phase, which rsync-copies the
`ios-arm64` slice into the build dir at BUILD time. The phase's declared
output (`…/XCFrameworkIntermediates/wasm_run_flutter/WasmRun.framework`,
from `wasm_run_flutter-xcframeworks-output-files.xcfilelist`) never matches
the real artifact — the vendored slices ship a bare `libwasm_run_dart.a`, no
framework bundle — so the phase's up-to-date bookkeeping is structurally
wrong for this vendored setup.

The build database that decides "is this script phase up to date" lives in
`~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/XCBuildData` (flutter passes only
`BUILD_DIR`, no `-derivedDataPath`), keyed by the checkout path — it is
**outside the repo**, survives the workspace `git clean -ffdx` every CI run
performs, and is **per self-hosted runner** (`fa-m5-1` vs `fa-m5-2` have
different checkout paths → different DerivedData). On runner `fa-m5-2` the
`fix/duo-header-folder-testflight` dispatch run started 2026-11-10 20:45 UTC
(run 42898409271) was cancelled mid-build; since then **every** build-ios on
`fa-m5-2` skips the Copy-XCFrameworks copy, `libwasm_run_dart.a` is absent
from `XCFrameworkIntermediates` at link time, and the link dies.

**Impact**: 6/6 consecutive `Build iOS` runs red on `fa-m5-2` since
21:13 UTC Nov 10 across three different trees (b153247, b9eba2a = v1.0.707
tag, plus the scheduled main builds), each ~identical error. The same tree
builds green on `fa-m5-1` (run 42907643431, 21:42) and on GitHub-hosted
macOS (v1.0.706 and earlier) — the repo config is fine; the failure is the
runner-state-dependent link dependency described above. Downstream: Quality
gate reds on the platform leg (#1368 semantics), the release train stops,
`Advance vpinned marker` fails its provenance gate (no SHA256SUMS published
for v1.0.707 — a deliberate fail-closed, gh-2070 class).

Evidence table (build-ios on the b9eba2a tree unless noted):

| run | time (UTC) | tree | runner | build-ios |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 42889653402 | 11-10 19:52 | ad5eeb5 | fa-m5-2 | PASS |
| 42903006339 | 11-10 21:13 | b153247 | fa-m5-2 | FAIL `Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found` |
| 42907643431 | 11-10 21:42 | 3a13a97 (≡ b9eba2a) | fa-m5-1 | PASS |
| 42914416457 | 11-10 22:25 | b9eba2a | fa-m5-2 | FAIL |
| 42933339085 | 11-11 00:41 | b9eba2a | fa-m5-2 | FAIL |
| 42945943836 | 11-11 02:25 | b9eba2a | fa-m5-2 | FAIL |
| 42959211250 | 11-11 04:26 | b9eba2a | fa-m5-2 | FAIL |
| 42965479924 | 11-11 05:29 | b9eba2a (tag v1.0.707) | fa-m5-2 | FAIL (this ticket) |

**Fix approach**: make the `-l"wasm_run_dart"` resolution independent of the
fragile `XCFrameworkIntermediates` copy. The Podfile `post_install` hook
already rewrites `OTHER_LDFLAGS[sdk=…]` per configuration to force_load the
exact restored slices; extend it to also inject
`LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=iphoneos*]` / `[sdk=iphonesimulator*]` pointing at
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/<slice>` — the
same paths the `-Wl,-force_load` and the post_install `nm` check already pin.
The injected path goes **before** `$(inherited)` so a stale/poisoned
intermediates copy can never satisfy the `-l` lookup with different bytes
than the force_load loads. The regenerated `project.pbxproj` is committed
(the pod-install-stable state, per the repo's pod-sync contract), and a new
guard test (`test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart`, in the style of
`test/wasmrun_macos_pod_link_test.dart`) pins the invariant.

The stale `fa-m5-2` DerivedData state becomes irrelevant with the fix, but
infra-side cleanup is still advisable (see `outputs/response.md` Notes):
`rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-*` on the fa-m5-2
registration clears the poisoned build database for every other target too.

**Previous attempt**: none — first development leg for gh-2106. (The
`fix/duo-header-folder-testflight` branch authored the self-hosted move of
this leg and the Duo shell itself; its content merged as #2092 = b9eba2a =
v1.0.707. That work is not a fix attempt for this failure — it introduced
the runner pool this failure class lives on and immediately tripped it.)

test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # gh-1778: 20 min — sized for the degraded-cache worst case, not just
    # the warm wall. Warm shards take ~460-525 s (run 39703080550) but the
    # v1.0.621 release run stalled ~133 s on EACH cache step (degraded
    # GitHub cache service, keys that existed) and needed ~14 min cold —
    # cancelled at the 12-min wall with 2535/2761 tests green, reding the

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

`Build iOS (debug, unsigned)` red on every self-hosted `fa-m5-2` run since the cancelled 2026-11-10 20:45 dispatch (6/6 runs, three different trees — green on `fa-m5-1` and GitHub-hosted with the identical v1.0.707 tree) with `Error (Xcode): Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found`. CocoaPods generates `-l"wasm_run_dart"` on the Runner link (from the vendored archive-slice `WasmRun.xcframework`), and its only search path is `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter` — a copy made at BUILD time by the pod's `[CP] Copy XCFrameworks` phase, whose declared output (`…/WasmRun.framework`) never matches the real bare-`.a` slice. That copy lives under a DerivedData build database outside the repo (survives the workspace `git clean -ffdx`, keyed per checkout path → per runner); the cancelled run poisoned `fa-m5-2`'s, the copy stopped landing, the `-l` lookup failed, the link died.

### Fix

- `flutter_app/ios/Podfile`: the `post_install` hook now also injects `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=iphoneos*]` / `[sdk=iphonesimulator*]` pointing at the restored `WasmRun.xcframework` slice dirs (vendored path first, before `$(inherited)`) — the same paths the existing `-Wl,-force_load` flags and the post_install `nm` check already pin — so ld resolves `-l"wasm_run_dart"` from the restored archive and never depends on the intermediates copy.
- `flutter_app/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`: regenerated via `pod install` and committed (pod-install-stable; carries the new settings for Debug/Release/Profile).
- `test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart`: new guard test in the `wasmrun_macos_pod_link_test.dart` style.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart` — 3/3 passed; verified RED before the fix (2 failures on the unmodified Podfile).
- Full root suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: 7535 passed, 0 failed (~16 min wall).
- `bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync` — pass; `pod install` re-run confirmed idempotent against the committed pbxproj.

### Notes

- No Dart/native product code changed — the Runner's force_load + exported-symbol machinery (TestFlight white-screen protection) is untouched and guarded by the new test's third assertion.
- The stale `fa-m5-2` DerivedData state on the box becomes irrelevant for this link; infra may still clear it for other targets: `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-*` on the `fa-m5-2` registration.
- The local `Podfile.lock` SPEC CHECKSUMS churn seen during development was a 3.47.9-vs-3.47.4 podspec-hash artifact of the dev sandbox and was reverted; CI pins 3.47.4 with `--enforce-lockfile`, so the committed lockfile is untouched.

diff --git a/flutter_app/ios/Podfile b/flutter_app/ios/Podfile
index fa56c18..0d3987d 100644
--- a/flutter_app/ios/Podfile
+++ b/flutter_app/ios/Podfile
@@ -137,6 +137,39 @@ post_install do |installer|
           ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
           config.build_settings[key] = ldflags
         end
+
+        # gh-2106: CocoaPods turns the vendored archive-slice XCFramework
+        # into -l"wasm_run_dart" on the Runner link (Pods-Runner.*.xcconfig
+        # OTHER_LDFLAGS), resolved ONLY through LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS'
+        # ${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter — a copy the
+        # wasm_run_flutter pod's "[CP] Copy XCFrameworks" phase rsyncs at
+        # BUILD time. That phase's DECLARED output
+        # (…/XCFrameworkIntermediates/wasm_run_flutter/WasmRun.framework)
+        # never matches the real artifact (the slices ship a bare
+        # libwasm_run_dart.a, no framework bundle), so on a self-hosted
+        # runner a cancelled build can poison the per-project DerivedData
+        # build database (~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData — keyed by
+        # the checkout path, OUTSIDE the repo, invisible to the workspace
+        # `git clean -ffdx`) and every later run skips the copy; the link
+        # then dies with "Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found"
+        # (v1.0.707, run 42965479924: 6/6 fa-m5-2 runs red since the
+        # cancelled 20:45 dispatch, same tree green on fa-m5-1 and hosted).
+        # Point the -l straight at the restored slices — the same paths the
+        # force_load flags and the post_install nm check already pin — so
+        # the link no longer depends on the intermediates copy at all.
+        # Search order puts the vendor slice before $(inherited) so a
+        # stale intermediates copy can never satisfy the -l lookup with
+        # different bytes than the force_load loaded.
+        device_slice_dir = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64"
+        simulator_slice_dir = "#{xcframework}/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator"
+        { 'iphoneos*' => device_slice_dir, 'iphonesimulator*' => simulator_slice_dir }.each do |sdk, slice_dir|
+          key = "LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=#{sdk}]"
+          paths = Array(config.build_settings[key] || []).dup
+          # Drop flags injected by earlier pod installs (idempotent re-runs).
+          paths.reject! { |p| p.include?('WasmRun.xcframework') }
+          paths.reject! { |p| p == '$(inherited)' }
+          config.build_settings[key] = [slice_dir, '$(inherited)', *paths]
+        end
       end
     end
   end

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

`Build iOS (debug, unsigned)` red on every self-hosted `fa-m5-2` run since the cancelled 2026-11-10 20:45 dispatch (6/6 runs, three different trees — green on `fa-m5-1` and GitHub-hosted with the identical v1.0.707 tree) with `Error (Xcode): Library 'wasm_run_dart' not found`. CocoaPods generates `-l"wasm_run_dart"` on the Runner link (from the vendored archive-slice `WasmRun.xcframework`), and its only search path is `${PODS_XCFRAMEWORKS_BUILD_DIR}/wasm_run_flutter` — a copy made at BUILD time by the pod's `[CP] Copy XCFrameworks` phase, whose declared output (`…/WasmRun.framework`) never matches the real bare-`.a` slice. That copy's build bookkeeping lives in a DerivedData build database outside the repo (survives the workspace `git clean -ffdx`, keyed per checkout path → per runner); the cancelled run poisoned `fa-m5-2`'s, the copy stopped landing, the `-l` lookup failed, the link died.

### Fix

- `flutter_app/ios/Podfile`: the `post_install` hook now also injects `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=iphoneos*]` / `[sdk=iphonesimulator*]` pointing at the restored `WasmRun.xcframework` slice dirs (vendored path first, before `$(inherited)`) — the same paths the existing `-Wl,-force_load` flags and the post_install `nm` check already pin — so ld resolves `-l"wasm_run_dart"` from the restored archive and never depends on the intermediates copy.
- `flutter_app/ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`: regenerated via `pod install` and committed (pod-install-stable; carries the new settings for Debug/Release/Profile).
- `test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart`: new guard test in the `wasmrun_macos_pod_link_test.dart` style.

### Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart` — 3/3 passed; verified RED before the fix (2 failures on the unmodified Podfile), and the pbxproj-sync assertion verified RED against a reverted pbxproj.
- Full root suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **13,770 passed, 0 failed** (SUITE_EXIT=0, ~12 min wall).
- `bash scripts/check_lockfiles.sh pod-sync` — pass; `pod install` re-run confirmed idempotent against the committed pbxproj; `ruby -c flutter_app/ios/Podfile` — syntax OK.

### Notes

- No Dart/native product code changed — the Runner's force_load + exported-symbol machinery (TestFlight white-screen protection) is untouched and pinned by the new test's third assertion.
- The stale `fa-m5-2` DerivedData state on the box becomes irrelevant for this link; infra may still clear it for other targets: `rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Runner-*` on the `fa-m5-2` registration.
- The local `Podfile.lock` SPEC CHECKSUMS churn seen during development was a 3.47.9-vs-3.47.4 podspec-hash artifact of the dev sandbox and was reverted; CI pins 3.47.4 with `--enforce-lockfile`, so the committed lockfile is untouched.

content.text:
All verification complete. Final summary of the work:

**Ticket gh-2106 `[ci-red] v1.0.707 failed`** — root-caused to a runner-state-dependent link failure in `Build iOS (debug, unsigned)`, fixed with a minimal, guarded change on branch `ai/gh-2106` @ `23a4cef`.

**Root cause (full chain):** CocoaPods generates `-l"wasm_run_dart"` on the Runner link from the vendored archive-slice `WasmRun.xcframework`; its only search path is the `XCFrameworkIntermediates` copy made at *build* time by the pod's `[CP] Copy XCFrameworks` phase — whose declared output (`WasmRun.framework`) never matches the real bare-`.a` slice. The build database deciding whether that phase runs lives in per-checkout-path DerivedData *outside the repo* (survives the workspace `git clean -ffdx`): a cancelled dispatch run (2026-11-10 20:45) poisoned `fa-m5-2`'s, the copy stopped landing, and **6/6 consecutive** `fa-m5-2` builds across three different trees died at link — while the identical tree stayed green on `fa-m5-1` and GitHub-hosted.

**Fix:** the Podfile `post_install` hook now injects `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS[sdk=iphoneos*]`/`[sdk=iphonesimulator*]` pointing at the restored xcframework slice dirs (vendored path first), so ld resolves the `-l` from the archive the force_load and `nm` check already pin — the intermediates dependency is gone entirely. pbxproj regenerated via `pod install` and committed (pod-install-stable, verified idempotent); new `test/wasmrun_ios_pod_link_test.dart` guard pins the invariant (RED pre-fix, GREEN post, negative-controlled).
